html:
Oil production off Bioko began in earnest in 1996, when an American company started pumping from the Zafiro field, and within a decade Equatorial Guinea was one of the larger oil producers south of the Sahara.

Before that the country lived on cocoa, timber and Spanish aid, and was among the poorest in Africa. Oil and gas made its income per head among the highest on the continent, paid for new roads, a new city on the mainland and grand buildings in Malabo.

The gains were narrowly shared. Courts in France and the United States pursued members of the ruling family over money from oil, and most people still lack clean water. Output began to fall in the 2010s, leaving the old question of what comes after oil.
